questions.solution: Turbidity is the measure of relative clarity of a liquid. questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Firstly, it provides air for respiration, serves the sense of smell and conditions the air by filtering, warming, and moistening it.

B. The nose is the prominent structure between the eyes that serves as the entrance to the respiratory tract.

C. For inhalation it has two cavities, separated from one another by a wall of cartilage called the septum.

D. Apart from filtering the air, it also cleans itself of foreign debris extracted from inhalations.
questions.solution: If we read all four sentences carefully, we notice that B should be clearly placed first as it introduces the subject matter of the paragraph, 'the nose'; the rest of the sentences have the pronoun 'it' in them. A should be placed next to B because it starts with the word 'firstly' which indicates that among many other things, this is the first thing the speaker wants the readers to know. D can be placed next to A because it further explains what the nose does apart from filtering as previously explained in A. C clearly forms the last sentence of the paragraph. Rearranging the sentences in the order of BADC forms a meaningful and coherent paragraph. Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. It has / been raining / since / two hours.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.

It has / been raining / since / two hours.
questions.solution: Option (a) has an error. 'Since' is used to situate an event in relation to a moment in time, but 'for' is used to relate the event to a period of time or duration. The given sentence mentions 'two hours' which is a duration of time. So, 'since' should be replaced by 'for' in order to rectify the error. Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'. In spite of my niece's dog Casper is very mischievous, he is lovable.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

In spite of my niece's dog Casper is very mischievous, he is lovable.
questions.solution: 'In spite of' is always placed in front of a noun or is followed by a gerund acting as a noun. 'Although' is a conjunction and is used at the beginning of a sentence. We use although to link two contrasting ideas or show that one fact makes the other fact surprising, which is also the case here in the given sentence as Casper is both mischievous and loveable. Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer. Every Saturday, / the workers gets / their weekly wages.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Every Saturday, / the workers gets / their weekly wages.
questions.solution: Option (b) has an error because it violates the subject-verb agreement rule. The noun given in the sentence, i.e., 'workers' is plural, so the verb used here should also be plural in form. In order to rectify the given error, 'gets' [singular] should be replaced by 'get'. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

'Are' [plural] in the given sentence should be replaced by 'is' [singular] in order to rectify the error. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'. Which movie have you watch on television when I called you?
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

Which movie have you watch on television when I called you?
questions.solution:
Except for special cases where the intended meaning requires a change in tense, it is advisable to maintain the same tense within a sentence. So, it would be more appropriate if the phrase 'have you watch' [present perfect tense] gets replaced by 'were you watching' [past continuous tense simultaneous with the point in time in the past when the person 'I' was on a call with the person 'you'].

Option (c) is negated despite being in the past tense because with 'did' only the base form of verb is used, which is not the case in this option. Option d) is negated because it is in the present continuous tense.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of the verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The question in Active voice is in interrogative form. These are "wh" questions that don't take "yes" or "no" as an answer.

"Who" is changed into "By whom?"

Also, the verb is placed before the subject in the Passive Voice.

For example:

Who teaches you Math? (Active)

By whom are you taught Math? (or) Who are you taught Math by? (Passive)

Also, the sentence is in the present continuous tense in Active voice. So, in the Passive voice, the present continuous tense should be used.

The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice. Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of the verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in the Past Indefinite. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Past Indefinite.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + V2 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Real Madrid won the Champions League. (Active Voice)

The Champions League was won by Real Madrid. (Passive Voice)

The options except (b) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.
